subject: math
title: Metric Units and Time: Converting Length, Mass and Capacity, and Elapsed Time
seo_title: Grade 6 Metric Units and Elapsed Time Worksheets: mm, cm, m, km, g, kg, mL, L (Free Math, Answer Key)
standard_text: Measure length, area, mass, and capacity using appropriate metric units, and solve problems that require converting smaller units to larger ones and vice versa; solve problems involving elapsed time
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on metric units and elapsed time for the Ontario curriculum: converting mm, cm, m and km, g and kg, mL and L with decimals, choosing the unit, and elapsed time across hours, with a Terry Fox Run and maple syrup word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide.
key_sub: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 L = 1000 mL. For time, an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so count on in jumps.
body_html:
Multiply or divide?

To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply: you need more of the small units. To change a smaller unit into a bigger unit, divide. Multiplying by 1000 moves every digit 3 places to the left. Dividing by 1000 moves every digit 3 places to the right.

MeasureFacts to know
Length1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm   1 km = 1000 m
Mass1 kg = 1000 g
Capacity1 L = 1000 mL
Time1 hour = 60 minutes   1 day = 24 hours
Example 1: metres to centimetres

1.25 m = ☐ cm

1 m = 100 cm. Multiply: 1.25 × 100 = 125.

Answer: 125 cm

Example 2: grams to kilograms

750 g = ☐ kg

1 kg = 1000 g. Divide: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75.

Answer: 0.75 kg

Example 3: two units as one decimal

3 kg 40 g = ☐ kg

40 g = 40 ÷ 1000 = 0.04 kg. Keep the 0 in the tenths place.

Answer: 3.04 kg (not 3.4 kg)

Read the scale, then convert

First find what one line on the scale is worth. Then read it and change the unit if you need to.

Choose the unit

Pick the unit that gives an easy number. A hockey stick is about 1.5 m, not 0.0015 km. An ant is 6 mm, not 0.006 m. Area always needs square units: cm², m² or km².

Elapsed time across hours

An hour has 60 minutes, so you cannot subtract clock times like ordinary numbers. Count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left. Remember that times change from a.m. to p.m. after 12 noon.

Example 4: finding the end time

A movie starts at 7:25 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. When does it end?

Add 1 hour: 7:25 p.m. + 1 h = 8:25 p.m. Then add 50 minutes: 35 minutes takes you to 9:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 9:15 p.m.

Answer: 9:15 p.m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2.5 kg = 250 g (multiplying by 100)1 kg = 1000 g, so 2.5 kg = 2500 g
750 g = 750 000 kg (moving the point the wrong way)Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide. 750 g = 0.75 kg
3 kg 40 g = 3.4 kg40 g = 0.04 kg, so 3 kg 40 g = 3.04 kg
9:40 to 11:15 is 1115 − 940 = 1 hour 75 minutes (100 minutes per hour)Count on: 20 minutes + 1 hour + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes
1.5 hours = 1 hour 50 minutesHalf an hour is 30 minutes: 1.5 hours = 90 minutes

faq.q: What metric conversions do Grade 6 students learn in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 6 students convert between mm, cm, m and km, between g and kg, and between mL and L, using decimals such as 1.25 m = 125 cm and 750 g = 0.75 kg. They also solve problems with elapsed time.

faq.q: How do you convert grams to kilograms?
faq.a: Divide by 1000, because 1 kg = 1000 g. So 750 g = 0.75 kg and 2600 g = 2.6 kg. To go from kilograms to grams, multiply by 1000.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to find elapsed time?
faq.a: Count on in jumps on a time line: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left. Do not subtract the clock numbers, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

faq.q: Are unit conversions and elapsed time on the Grade 6 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and measurement is part of the Spatial Sense strand. Practising conversions and elapsed time is good preparation.

sets.title: Length: mm, cm, m and km with decimals

items.q: Convert. 3.6 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 3.6 × 100 = 360. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 3.6 m = 360 cm.

items.q: Convert. 1.25 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.25 × 100 = 125. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.25 m = 125 cm.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.5 × 100 = 150. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.5 m = 150 cm. (1.5 m is 1 m 50 cm, so it is not 105 cm. 105 cm would be 1.05 m.)

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so divide by 10: 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. The digits move 1 place to the right. So 45 mm = 4.5 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2.4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 2.4 × 1000 = 2400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 km = 2400 m.

items.q: Convert. 850 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 850 ÷ 1000 = 0.85. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 850 m = 0.85 km. (850 000 km multiplies when it should divide.)

items.q: Convert. 0.7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 0.7 × 10 = 7. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 0.7 cm = 7 mm.

items.q: Convert. 65 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 65 ÷ 100 = 0.65. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 65 cm = 0.65 m.
The pencil ends 3 small marks after 8 cm. Each small mark is 1 mm, so it is 83 mm. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 83 ÷ 10 = 8.3 cm.
The crayon starts at 1 cm, not at 0. It ends 6 small marks after 7 cm, at 7.6 cm. 7.6 − 1 = 6.6 cm (66 mm). 7.6 cm is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Convert. 3.125 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 3.125 × 1000 = 3125. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.125 km = 3125 m.

items.q: Convert. 75 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 75 ÷ 1000 = 0.075. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 75 m = 0.075 km. Check: 0.75 km would be 750 m.

items.q: Convert. 1.75 m = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm. Metres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 1000: 1.75 × 1000 = 1750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.75 m = 1750 mm. (1.75 × 100 = 175 gives centimetres, not millimetres.)

items.q: Convert. 38 mm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm. Millimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 1000: 38 ÷ 1000 = 0.038. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 38 mm = 0.038 m. You need a 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: Convert. 4050 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1000: 4050 ÷ 1000 = 4.05. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 4050 m = 4.05 km. The 0 in 4050 keeps its place: 4.05, not 4.5.

items.q: Convert. 1.08 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.08 × 100 = 108. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.08 m = 108 cm.

items.q: The CN Tower in Toronto is 553 m tall. How tall is it in kilometres?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so divide by 1000: 553 ÷ 1000 = 0.553 km. The digits move 3 places to the right. (5.53 km divides by 100, and 553 000 km multiplies.)

items.q: Convert. 2 km 75 m = ☐ km
Which is the same as 6.04 m?
Find the missing number. 1 km − 375 m = ☐ km

sets.title: Mass and capacity: g, kg, mL and L

items.q: Convert. 750 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 g = 0.75 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2.5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 2.5 × 1000 = 2500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.5 kg = 2500 g. (250 g multiplies by 100, but 1 kg is 1000 g, not 100 g.)

items.q: Convert. 3.2 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 3.2 × 1000 = 3200. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.2 kg = 3200 g. (320 g uses × 100. A kilogram has 1000 grams.)

items.q: Convert. 1.25 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 1.25 × 1000 = 1250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.25 L = 1250 mL. (125 mL would be 0.125 L.)

items.q: Convert. 330 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1000: 330 ÷ 1000 = 0.33. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 330 mL = 0.33 L.

items.q: Convert. 0.5 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.5 × 1000 = 500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.5 L = 500 mL. (50 mL uses × 100. A litre has 1000 millilitres.)

items.q: Convert. 45 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 45 ÷ 1000 = 0.045. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 45 g = 0.045 kg.

items.q: Convert. 4.08 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 4.08 × 1000 = 4080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4.08 kg = 4080 g.

items.q: Convert. 2600 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1000: 2600 ÷ 1000 = 2.6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 2600 mL = 2.6 L.

items.q: Convert. 0.08 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.08 × 1000 = 80. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.08 L = 80 mL.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 50 g = 50 ÷ 1000 = 0.05 kg. So 3 kg 50 g = 3.05 kg. 3.5 kg would be 3 kg 500 g.

items.q: Convert. 1 L 200 mL = ☐ L
The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 kg (200 g). The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0.4 = 1.4 kg. (1.2 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a box of books. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0.75 = 2.75 kg. (2.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some apples. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The needle points to 600 g. 1 kg = 1000 g, so divide by 1000: 600 ÷ 1000 = 0.6 kg.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL with 5 spaces between them, so each line is 100 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1000 mL: 1300 mL. 1300 ÷ 1000 = 1.3 L. (1.03 L would be 1030 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL with 5 spaces between them, so each line is 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 500 mL: 500 + 150 = 650 mL. 650 ÷ 1000 = 0.65 L. (0.53 L counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL. The water is at 1600 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1600 = 400 mL more. (600 mL reads the water level as 1400 mL.)

items.q: Work out 1.5 kg + 700 g. Give your answer in kilograms.
items.e: Use one unit first: 700 g = 0.7 kg. Then 1.5 + 0.7 = 2.2 kg. 701.5 kg adds the numbers without converting, and 8.5 kg treats 700 g as 7 kg.

items.q: Work out 4 L − 1750 mL. Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: Use one unit first: 4 L = 4000 mL. 4000 − 1750 = 2250 mL. (1746 mL takes away 4 without converting, and 5750 mL adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bag of potatoes?
items.e: Mass is measured in grams or kilograms. A bag of potatoes is heavy, so kilograms fit. Litres measure capacity, and kilometres and millimetres measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a skating rink?
items.e: A skating rink is about 60 m long, so metres fit. A kilometre is far too long, a millimetre far too small, and grams measure mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a classroom floor?
items.e: Area needs square units. A classroom floor is about 8 m by 9 m, so square metres fit. Metres measure length, not area.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a postage stamp?
items.e: A stamp is small and flat, about 3 cm by 4 cm, so square centimetres fit. Centimetres alone measure length, not area.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of Lake Ontario?
items.e: Lake Ontario is huge, so square kilometres fit. Kilometres alone measure length, not area.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of an adult moose?
items.e: An adult moose is much heavier than a person, so hundreds of kilograms fit. 4.5 kg is about the mass of a cat.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much a juice box holds?
items.e: A juice box holds much less than a litre. 200 mL = 0.2 L. 2 L is a big carton.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the length of a hockey stick?
items.e: A hockey stick comes up to about a student’s chin, so 1.5 m fits. 1.5 cm is shorter than a fingernail, and 15 m is longer than a school bus.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the driving distance from Toronto to Ottawa?
items.e: Toronto to Ottawa is a drive of about 4 or 5 hours, so it is a few hundred kilometres. 4.5 km is only about an hour’s walk.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the thickness of a loonie?
items.e: A loonie is very thin, less than 1 cm, so millimetres fit. 2 cm is as thick as a stack of about 10 loonies.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so litres fit. 1.5 L is only a large water bottle.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a Grade 6 student?
items.e: Most Grade 6 students have a mass of about 30 kg to 50 kg. 4 kg is about the mass of a new baby.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a slice of bread?
items.e: A slice of bread is light, so grams fit. 0.3 kg = 300 g, which is about a whole small loaf.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much a teaspoon holds?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a tiny amount, so millilitres fit. 0.5 L = 500 mL, which is a whole bottle of water.

items.q: Owen jumps 312 cm in the long jump. Which shows this in metres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so divide by 100: 312 ÷ 100 = 3.12 m. The digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: A bag of rice has a mass of 1650 g. Which shows this in kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so divide by 1000: 1650 ÷ 1000 = 1.65 kg. (16.5 kg divides by 100, as if 1 kg were 100 g.)

items.q: An ant is 0.006 m long. Which shows the same length in a more sensible unit?
items.e: 1 m = 1000 mm, so 0.006 × 1000 = 6 mm. A small number of millimetres is easier to read than a decimal with zeros.

items.q: A newborn baby has a mass of 3 kg 40 g. Which shows this in kilograms?
items.e: 40 g = 40 ÷ 1000 = 0.04 kg. So 3 kg 40 g = 3.04 kg. 3.4 kg would be 3 kg 400 g.

items.q: A cross-country ski trail is 1 km 60 m long. Which shows this in kilometres?
items.e: 60 m = 60 ÷ 1000 = 0.06 km. So 1 km 60 m = 1.06 km. 1.6 km would be 1 km 600 m.

items.q: A pot holds 2 L 50 mL of soup. Which shows this in litres?
How long is 135 minutes in hours and minutes?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 135 − 60 − 60 = 15, so 135 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (1 hour 35 minutes treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: How many minutes are in 2.5 hours?
items.e: 2.5 hours = 2 hours and half an hour. 2 × 60 + 30 = 150 minutes. (250 uses 100 minutes per hour, and 170 reads 2.5 hours as 2 hours 50 minutes.)

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 1.5 hours = 90 minutes and 1 hour 20 minutes = 80 minutes. 100 minutes is the longest. (1.5 hours is 1 hour 30 minutes, not 1 hour 50 minutes.)

items.q: A class trip to the museum leaves at 9:40 a.m. and arrives at 11:15 a.m. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 9:40 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 20 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 11:00 a.m. to 11:15 a.m. is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A soccer game starts at 2:50 p.m. and ends at 4:05 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on: 2:50 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 4:00 p.m. to 4:05 p.m. is 5 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 5 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Hockey practice runs from 6:45 a.m. to 8:10 a.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on: 6:45 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. is 15 minutes; 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 8:00 a.m. to 8:10 a.m. is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The time line shows a school concert rehearsal. How long is it from 10:45 a.m. to 1:20 p.m.?
items.e: Count on: 10:45 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 15 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 1:00 p.m. to 1:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 2 hours + 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes.

items.q: The time line shows a math and science fair. How long is it from 9:35 a.m. to 12:20 p.m.?
items.e: Count on: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 2 hours; 12:00 noon to 12:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes.

items.q: The time line shows a skating party. How long is it from 2:35 p.m. to 5:15 p.m.?
items.e: Count on: 2:35 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 25 minutes; 3:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 5:00 p.m. to 5:15 p.m. is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 40 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Leah’s family drives to the cottage. They leave at 11:30 a.m. and arrive at 2:10 p.m. How long is the drive?
items.e: Count on: 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 30 minutes; 12:00 noon to 2:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 2:00 p.m. to 2:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 30 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 40 minutes.

items.q: Work out 1 hour 45 minutes + 50 minutes.
items.e: 45 + 50 = 95 minutes. 95 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes, so the total is 1 hour + 1 hour 35 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes. (1 hour 35 minutes forgets to carry the extra hour.)

items.q: A movie starts at 7:25 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 7:25 p.m. + 1 h = 8:25 p.m. Then add 50 minutes: 35 minutes takes you to 9:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 9:15 p.m.

items.q: Mateo’s canoe trip starts at 10:35 a.m. He paddles for 2 hours 50 minutes. What time does he finish?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 10:35 a.m. + 2 h = 12:35 p.m. Then add 50 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 1:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 1:25 p.m.

items.q: The school bus must arrive by 8:40 a.m. The ride takes 55 minutes. What is the latest time the bus can leave?
items.e: Count back 55 minutes: 40 minutes takes you to 8:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 7:45 a.m.

items.q: Arjun’s swimming lesson ends at 5:05 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 20 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 4:05 p.m. Then count back 20 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 4:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 3:45 p.m.

items.q: A train leaves Toronto at 9:40 a.m. The trip to Ottawa takes 4 hours 25 minutes. What time does the train arrive?
items.e: Add 4 hours: 9:40 a.m. + 4 h = 1:40 p.m. Then add 25 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 5 minutes more is 2:05 p.m.

items.q: A flight from Toronto to Vancouver takes off at 8:15 a.m. Toronto time. It is in the air for 5 hours 10 minutes. What time is it in Toronto when the plane lands?
items.e: Add 5 hours: 8:15 a.m. + 5 h = 1:15 p.m. Then add 10 minutes: 1:25 p.m.

items.q: Clocks in Vancouver are 3 hours behind clocks in Toronto. A plane lands in Vancouver at 1:25 p.m. Toronto time. What time do the clocks in Vancouver show?
items.e: Vancouver is behind, so count back 3 hours: 1:25 p.m. → 12:25 p.m. → 11:25 a.m. → 10:25 a.m. Going back past 12 o’clock changes p.m. to a.m. (4:25 p.m. adds the 3 hours instead.)

items.q: A flight from Toronto to Vancouver takes off at 5:50 p.m. and lands at 10:55 p.m., both in Toronto time. How long is the flight?
items.e: Count on: 5:50 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. is 4 hours; 10:00 p.m. to 10:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 4 hours + 10 minutes + 55 minutes = 5 hours 5 minutes.

items.q: Hana goes to bed at 9:15 p.m. and wakes up at 6:45 a.m. How long does she sleep?
items.e: Do not just subtract 6:45 from 9:15: the time goes past midnight. Count on: 9:15 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. is 45 minutes; 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. is 8 hours; 6:00 a.m. to 6:45 a.m. is 45 minutes. 8 hours + 45 minutes + 45 minutes = 9 hours 30 minutes.

sets.title: Word problems: Terry Fox Run, maple syrup and trips

items.q: Our school’s Terry Fox Run is 5 km. Students run laps of a 400 m track. How many laps is 5 km?
items.e: 5 km = 5000 m. 5000 ÷ 400 = 12.5 laps. Check: 12 × 400 = 4800 m, and half a lap is 200 m more.

items.q: Maya has run 3.2 km of the 5 km Terry Fox Run. How many metres does she have left?
The Terry Fox Run starts at 1:40 p.m. Chloe runs the 5 km in 38 minutes. What time does she finish?
items.e: Add 38 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 18 minutes more is 2:18 p.m. (1:18 p.m. forgets to move on to the next hour.)

items.q: A sugar shack has 15 L of maple syrup. It fills bottles that hold 250 mL each. How many bottles can it fill?
items.e: 15 L = 15 000 mL. 15 000 ÷ 250 = 60 bottles. Check: 4 bottles make 1 L, and 15 × 4 = 60. (6 bottles uses 15 L = 1500 mL, and 3750 multiplies 15 × 250.)

items.q: A family buys 6 bottles of maple syrup. Each bottle holds 250 mL. How many litres of syrup is that?
It takes about 40 L of maple sap to make 1 L of maple syrup. About how much sap is needed for 750 mL of syrup?
items.e: 750 mL = 0.75 L. 40 × 0.75 = 30 L of sap. (30 000 L multiplies 40 × 750 without changing 750 mL into litres.)

items.q: Liam packs his hockey bag: skates 1.6 kg, helmet 650 g and pads 2.35 kg. What is the total mass in kilograms?
items.e: Change 650 g to kilograms first: 650 ÷ 1000 = 0.65 kg. 1.6 + 0.65 + 2.35 = 4.6 kg. (653.95 kg adds without converting, and 10.45 kg treats 650 g as 6.5 kg.)

items.q: Ethan makes pancakes. Each batch needs 0.3 kg of flour. He makes 3 batches from a 1.5 kg bag. How many grams of flour are left?
items.e: 3 × 0.3 = 0.9 kg used. 1.5 − 0.9 = 0.6 kg left. 0.6 × 1000 = 600 g. (1200 g only takes away one batch.)

items.q: A bird feeder holds 125 g of seed. How many times can Sofia fill it from a 2 kg bag?
A recipe for 4 people uses 250 mL of milk. How many litres of milk are needed for 10 people?
items.e: 250 ÷ 4 = 62.5 mL for each person. 10 × 62.5 = 625 mL. 625 ÷ 1000 = 0.625 L. (2.5 L uses 250 mL for each person.)

items.q: 25 students each bring a 750 mL water bottle on a field trip. How many litres of water is that altogether?
items.e: 25 × 750 = 18 750 mL. 18 750 ÷ 1000 = 18.75 L. (187.5 L divides by 100, and 18 750 L forgets to change millilitres into litres.)

items.q: A 2 L carton of juice is poured into 8 cups of 180 mL each. How many millilitres are left in the carton?
items.e: 8 × 180 = 1440 mL poured. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1440 = 560 mL left. (1820 mL takes away only one cup.)

items.q: Kai swims 1.2 km at practice in a 25 m pool. How many lengths does he swim?
items.e: 1.2 km = 1200 m. 1200 ÷ 25 = 48 lengths. Check: 48 × 25 = 1200. (24 lengths counts there and back, 50 m, as one length.)

items.q: Zoe has 4.5 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces 15 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 4.5 m = 450 cm. 450 ÷ 15 = 30 pieces. (3 pieces divides 45 by 15 without converting.)

items.q: A canoe route is 12 km. The group paddles 2.75 km before lunch and 3600 m after lunch. How much farther do they still have to paddle?
items.e: 3600 m = 3.6 km. 2.75 + 3.6 = 6.35 km paddled. 12 − 6.35 = 5.65 km to go. (8.89 km treats 3600 m as 0.36 km, and 6.35 km is the distance already paddled.)

items.q: A box of 24 apples has a mass of 3.6 kg. Each apple has the same mass. What is the mass of one apple in grams?
items.e: 3.6 kg = 3600 g. 3600 ÷ 24 = 150 g. (15 g changes 3.6 kg into 360 g, and 86.4 g multiplies 3.6 × 24.)

items.q: Ava was 1.38 m tall last year. Since then she has grown 6 cm. How tall is she now, in metres?
The field trip bus leaves school at 8:50 a.m. and arrives at the science centre at 10:35 a.m. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on: 8:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 10 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 10:00 a.m. to 10:35 a.m. is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Nathan’s family leaves home at 6:20 a.m. The drive to the airport takes 1 hour 15 minutes. Their flight to Vancouver leaves 2 hours 30 minutes after they arrive. What time does the flight leave?
items.e: Arrive at the airport: 6:20 a.m. + 1 hour 15 minutes = 7:35 a.m. Then 7:35 a.m. + 2 hours = 9:35 a.m., and 30 minutes more is 10:05 a.m. (7:35 a.m. is when they reach the airport, not when the flight leaves.)

items.q: Priya walks 1.5 km to the rink. She walks 1 km in about 12 minutes. She leaves home at 3:52 p.m. About what time does she reach the rink?
items.e: 1.5 km takes 12 + 6 = 18 minutes (half a kilometre takes half of 12 minutes). 3:52 p.m. + 8 minutes = 4:00 p.m., and 10 more minutes is 4:10 p.m. (4:04 p.m. adds only the 12 minutes for 1 km, and 4:07 p.m. uses 15 minutes instead of 18.)
